A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPEAK EASY and HarmScore. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and reorganized material.

before.justification: V1 reports original human-annotation studies, response-selection evaluations, experiments on three LLMs across four benchmarks, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds GPT-4o Past Tense Attack comparisons and additional metrics for the fixed-language analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a Past Tense Attack + SPEAK EASY variant that reformulates the original query before decomposition. The core decomposition, translation, response selection, concatenation, and model-training procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use HarmBench, AdvBench, SORRY-Bench, MedSafetyBench, the same preference-training datasets, and the same language coverage. The added attack comparison reuses existing benchmark tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Past Tense Attack, evaluated both alone and with SPEAK EASY on GPT-4o in Table 10. DR, GCG-T, TAP-T, and the response-selection model comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The added Past Tense experiments use GPT-4o, a three-shot reformulation prompt, and one reformulation attempt per query (Appendix B.3). Existing dataset splits, decoding settings, metrics, training settings, and ablation configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing fixed-language selection analysis with ASR and HarmScore for each of six languages in Table 12. V1 already reported their actionability, informativeness, and response rates in Table 11. Other ablation questions and analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The human-annotation counts, chi-square tests, Fleiss' kappa, and correlation reporting are unchanged. The added attack results introduce no repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or additional significance tests.

E6.justification: All existing Table 10 results are retained. New GPT-4o Past Tense rows report average ASR of 0.346 alone and 0.561 with SPEAK EASY, and HarmScore of 0.406 and 0.692, respectively. Table 12 additionally reports per-language ASR and HarmScore; Table 11's added metric columns reproduce existing Table 4 results.

T1.justification: The HarmScore definition in Section 3.2, response-selection rule in Section 4.1, and Bradley-Terry likelihood and training loss in Appendix B.2 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about actionability and informativeness, HarmScore's human alignment, and simple multilingual, multi-step jailbreaks. The headline average gains remain 0.319 in ASR and 0.426 in HarmScore.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds an interpretation linking high-resource languages to greater vulnerability, citing Chinese's highest fixed-language ASR and English's highest HarmScore. It also explicitly states that computational constraints restricted the new Past Tense comparison to GPT-4o.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds Past Tense implementation settings and expands the GCG-T/TAP-T integration instructions. Section 4.2 clarifies GPT-4o binary labeling, preference-pair construction, and continuous scoring. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware information, and code access are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Past Tense Attack, RewardBench, Liu et al. (2023), and Robey et al. (2023), including a RewardBench-based rationale for choosing reward-model baselines. The overall research positioning remains stable; publication updates to existing references do not represent new works.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited main-text clarifications, expands and rewrites the baseline explanations in Appendix B.3, and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 10, splits v1's Table 11 into Tables 11-12, and adds ASR and HarmScore columns. It clarifies Table 2's caption and adjusts table placement and front matter. The figures are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The added GPT-4o Past Tense comparison provides further evidence for integration with another attack, while the per-language metrics clarify v1's fixed-language summary. Expanded implementation explanations make the work easier to assess and reproduce. These are limited gains: the central results and validation remain unchanged, and the additional comparator is evaluated on only one model.
